target: values: suborbicular, ovate (FLOPO_0991024), elliptic (PATO_0000947), obovate (PATO_0001936), ovate-elliptic; value_qualifier 'approximately' only on orbicular; bearer leaf lamina (PO_0020039)
fix: A prefix 'sub-' on one item in a list of alternatives qualifies only that item. It should not set 'approximately' for the whole list. Also, the head word 'Leaf-lamina' should give the bearer leaf lamina, not leaf.
reason: The 'sub' of 'suborbicular' was spread to ovate, elliptic and obovate, which the flora gives exactly. Suborbicular and ovate-elliptic were dropped. The flora describes the lamina, not the whole leaf.

fix: 'jusqu'à X de long sous le fruit' (up to X long under the fruit) means the size in the fruiting stage. Add a stage slot and read 'jusqu'à' as an upper bound.
reason: In flower the same sepals are 2–3 mm. They reach 8–12 mm only under the fruit (accrescent), so without the stage the annotation contradicts the 2–3 mm figure.

fix: In 'basal blade X; cauline becoming Y distally', 'cauline' and 'distally' limit Y to the upper stem leaves. Carry them as context.
reason: The basal blades are obovate, oblanceolate or spatulate. Only the distal cauline blades are narrowly ovate or nearly linear.
'petals ... usually numerous' (double flowers of a garden plant). Petals present, many, usually.
The stem is tomentose (with stellate hairs) in its apical part. The part restriction is right.
'Fruit huge' (up to 60 cm) means increased size of the fruit.

fix: When a leaf description reads 'apex acute or acuminate', the bearer should be the leaf apex, as is already done for 'apex acute' on sepals (A01795).
reason: The flora gives acute or acuminate for the apex of the leaf blade, not for the blade as a whole.
'Shrub or tree': shrubby or tree habit, as alternatives.

fix: 'teeth' right after 'Calyx' means the calyx lobes (teeth) of a fused calyx, not whole sepals.
reason: The calyx is 10–12 mm and its teeth are 4–6 mm. The 4–6 mm is the free tooth, not the full sepal.

target: decreased length (PATO_0000574) relative to internode, ratio 0.5–0.6
fix: 'a/b–c/d as long as X' (shorter than X) is a relative length: decreased length towards X with the ratio. Without the ratio and the part it is compared with, it says nothing.
reason: The annotation keeps only 'has a length'. It loses that culm sheaths are half to three-fifths as long as the internodes.

fix: Cactus spines (radial and central spines on areoles) are modified leaves. Map them to spine leaf, not to thorn (a modified shoot).
reason: The quality 'subterete' is right, but PO 'thorn' is the wrong kind of spine for a cactus.
Flowers horizontal (PATO_0001855) or slightly erect (PATO_0000622), as alternatives.
Bracts numerous: present, many.

fix: 'the blade of the lowest [bract] exceeding the culm' is limited to the lowest bract. Keep 'lowest' as a position slot.
reason: Only the lowest bract exceeds the culm, not bracts in general.
'Bracteoles and sepals ... inside glabrous': the adaxial side of the sepal is glabrous.
Branchlets are quadrangular when young, and the context slot says 'young'.
The pappus bristles are sometimes lacking: pappus absent, sometimes.
The leaf blade is yellowish green when young.

target: cell wall of the hyaline cells of the leaf (no PO term)
fix: 'with wall thinnings' describes thin spots in the cell walls, not a thinner leaf.
reason: The thinnings are in the hyaline cell walls on the concave surface, in the cell corners. The leaf itself is not said to be thin.
The racemes are 20–50-flowered: 20–50 flowers per raceme.
The persistent calyx is 4-lobed: 4 calyx lobes.

fix: 'X mm thick' should map to thickness, which the size shapes expect, not to depth.
reason: The seed is 2 mm thick. PATO thickness is the quality the patterns use for this.
25–37 leaflets.
In 'Fruit 0,5-1,5 × 0,5-0,6 mm' the second figure, 0.5–0.6 mm, is the width.

fix: A sentence starting 'Distalmost stem leaves ...' limits its shapes to those leaves. Carry the position.
reason: The other leaf blades are ovate or oblong. Only the distalmost stem leaves are ovate-lanceolate.
The sepal apex is acute.

target: white to blue, or pink, or purple
fix: In 'A to B, C or D', the items after the comma are further alternatives. They must be kept beside the A–B range.
reason: Only white→blue was kept. Pink and purple were dropped.

fix: 'peduncle' should map to peduncle (inflorescence stem), not pedicel.
reason: The flora speaks of the stalk of the inflorescence, not of the flower stalk.

fix: Statements under 'Basal leaves in rosettes, ...' apply to the basal leaves only.
reason: The flora says the basal rosette leaves stay (withered) at anthesis, not all leaves.
The leaf blade narrows (attenuate) at the base into the petiole.
